title: Emery Worldwide 17
summary: An Emery Worldwide Douglas DC-8-71F took off from Sacramento Mather Airport on February 16, 2000. At approximately V1 speed during takeoff, the pitch increased from 0.2 to 5.3 degrees. The crew applied continuous nose-down input during takeoff roll but the nose continued rising from 14.5 to 17.4 degrees. Immediately after lift-off the first officer requested return to Sacramento. The aircraft entered a left turn with decreasing engine speed and stick shaker activated. The captain declared an emergency, the aircraft descended with increasing bank angle. The aircraft crashed into an automobile salvage yard shortly after takeoff.
probable_cause: During aircraft rotation, a control rod to the right elevator control tab detached, causing loss of pitch control. An incorrect maintenance procedure by Emery Worldwide introduced improper torque-loading on bolts securing the control rod (p. 83)

recommendations.text: Ensure DC-8 elevator position indicator gauges are properly installed and that crews are trained in their use for flight control checks
Require inspection and testing of DC-8 elevator control tab attachment bolts and ensure proper torque procedures in all maintenance protocols
Review DC-8 elevator control tab design to address potential failure modes and consider design improvements to prevent future detachment
